name: chain_timer
description: Scale spec §9 chain_timer. One instance per piece of due-time work the chain made due: settlement publishes chain.timer_scheduled when it sees the chain event (a cycle's end, a loan that can default, a delegation's activation or expiry, a member holding credit at a cycle's start). The instance waits until due_at and calls SettlementService.RunDue once. Settlement simulates the call and relays it only if it would succeed; work the chain says is not yet due is rescheduled by settlement as a new timer, so this instance never loops and nothing polls rooms. Protocol-scoped: it acts on the chain's own schedule, not on a room's pinned policy.

input.kind: cycle_close | member_settle | loan_default | loan_recover | delegation_activate | delegation_expire
input.ref: identifies the work; RunDue is idempotent by (kind, ref)
input.due_at: RFC 3339 timestamp: when the chain says the work is due

steps.name: WAITING — until the time the chain named
RUNNING — settlement simulates and relays the call once (ENQUEUED), reschedules it as a new timer (NOT_DUE), or finds it done (NOTHING_TO_DO)
STALLED (terminal) — RunDue failed after retries; the next chain event about this work sets a new timer, and anyone may still make the call

input.message: chain timer stalled: RunDue failed after retries
